description: Imagine the sun-drenched Ligurian coast, and you will taste this Focaccia Genovese. This classic Italian bread, celebrated for its irresistible crisp crust and airy, tender interior, is generously infused with fragrant rosemary and rich olive oil. It is a simple yet profound culinary delight, perfect for sharing as an appetizer or alongside any meal.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active. This is the first step to a wonderfully airy focaccia.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Gradually add 30ml of the extra virgin olive oil, kneading it into the dough until fully incorporated and the dough is smooth and elastic, about 8-10 minutes. It will be quite sticky.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil. Transfer the dough to the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size. Patience is key for a light texture.

instructions.title: Prepare for Baking
instructions.text: Generously oil a 9x13 inch baking pan with extra virgin olive oil. Gently transfer the risen dough into the prepared pan. Using your fingertips, gently stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. If the dough resists, let it rest for 10 minutes, then continue stretching.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Dimpling
instructions.text: Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap and let the dough rise for another 30-45 minutes. Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Once risen, remove the plastic wrap. Drizzle the remaining 30ml of olive oil over the dough. Using your oiled fingertips, gently press deep dimples all over the surface of the focaccia. In a small bowl, whisk together the 30ml water and 15ml olive oil for the brine. Pour this mixture evenly over the dimpled focaccia. Sprinkle with chopped fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Bake in the preheated oven for 20-30 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown and cooked through. The crust should be crisp and the interior soft and airy. Keep an eye on it to prevent over-browning.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven. If desired, drizzle with a little more fresh extra virgin olive oil for extra flavor and shine. Let it cool in the pan for a few minutes before transferring it to a wire rack to cool completely. Slice and serve warm or at room temperature. Buon appetito!

tips: Always use high-quality extra virgin olive oil; it truly makes a difference in the flavor and aroma of your focaccia. Do not be shy with it!
For an even airier crumb, consider using a '00' flour if available, though all-purpose flour works wonderfully too. The key is gentle handling of the dough.
Focaccia is best enjoyed the day it is made. If you have leftovers, refresh them in a warm oven for a few minutes to restore their crispness.
article:
The aroma of freshly baked bread, golden and glistening with olive oil, beckons from the heart of Italian kitchens. Among the pantheon of beloved Italian baked goods, one stands out for its elegant simplicity and profound flavor: Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil. This isn't just any focaccia; it's a culinary masterpiece from Genoa, the capital of Liguria, where the sea breeze carries the scent of pine and herbs. Imagine a flatbread with a delicate, crisp crust, a remarkably airy and moist interior, generously dimpled and kissed with fragrant rosemary and coarse sea salt. It’s a testament to how a few high-quality ingredients, handled with care, can create something truly extraordinary. If you’ve ever dreamed of bringing the authentic taste of Italy into your home, mastering the art of Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is an incredibly rewarding journey.

## What is Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil?

Focaccia Genovese is a traditional Ligurian flatbread, distinct from other focaccia varieties found across Italy. Its defining characteristics are its thinness, a remarkably light and airy crumb, and a generous amount of extra virgin olive oil both in the dough and drizzled over the top before baking. Unlike some focaccias that can be thick and heavily topped, the Genovese version celebrates simplicity, allowing the quality of its core ingredients to shine. The surface is famously dimpled, creating pockets where the olive oil pools, frying the dough slightly to achieve an irresistible crispy texture.

The addition of fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt elevates this focaccia from mere bread to a sensory experience. The rosemary infuses the dough with its aromatic, slightly piney notes, while the salt provides a crucial counterpoint, enhancing all the flavors. When you bite into a piece of Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil, you're met with a delicate crunch, followed by a soft, almost cloud-like interior, bursting with savory, herbaceous, and slightly briny flavors. It’s a versatile bread, perfect on its own, as an accompaniment, or as the base for a delicious sandwich.

## Ingredients You Need for Focaccia Genovese

Crafting authentic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil requires a commitment to quality ingredients, as their simplicity means there's nowhere for poor quality to hide.

*   **Strong Bread Flour (or '00' Flour):** About 500g. High-protein flour is crucial for developing the gluten structure needed for that airy, chewy crumb. '00' flour, if available, offers a wonderfully fine texture.
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** 7g (one standard packet). Ensures a good rise and light texture.
*   **Warm Water:** 350-400ml. The exact amount can vary slightly depending on your flour and humidity. It should be warm to the touch (around 105-115°F or 40-46°C) to activate the yeast.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** At least 100ml for the dough, plus more for the pan, drizzling, and finishing. This is perhaps the most important ingredient. Invest in a high-quality, fruity, peppery extra virgin olive oil.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** 10g (about 1.5 teaspoons) for the dough.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt (Maldon or flaky):** For sprinkling on top. This adds texture and bursts of briny flavor.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** 2-3 sprigs. Finely chopped for the dough, and whole leaves or small sprigs for the topping. Avoid dried rosemary if possible, as the fresh offers superior aroma and flavor.
*   **Pinch of Sugar:** Optional, but helps activate the yeast.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil

Making Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a joyful process that rewards patience.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a small bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar (if using). Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** In a large bowl, combine the flour and fine sea salt. Pour in the activated yeast mixture and 50ml of the extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
3.  **Knead:** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 10-15 minutes until it's smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. The dough should be quite wet and soft, so don't be tempted to add too much extra flour. If using a stand mixer with a dough hook, knead on medium speed for 8-10 minutes. Incorporate the finely chopped fresh rosemary during the last few minutes of kneading.
4.  **First Proof:** Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Generously coat a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan with extra virgin olive oil. Don't skimp here; this contributes to the crispy bottom crust.
6.  **Transfer and Stretch:** Gently turn the risen dough into the prepared pan. Using oiled hands, carefully stretch the dough to fill the pan, trying not to deflate it too much. If the dough resists, let it rest for 10 minutes, then continue stretching.
7.  **Second Proof:** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel and let it rise again for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C) during this time.
8.  **Dimple and Top:** Once risen, remove the cover. Using your oiled fingertips, gently but firmly press dimples all over the surface of the dough. These indentations are crucial for the focaccia's texture and for holding the olive oil. Drizzle generously with another 30-50ml of extra virgin olive oil, ensuring it pools in the dimples. Scatter fresh rosemary leaves or small sprigs and a good sprinkle of coarse sea salt over the entire surface.
9.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is golden brown on top and cooked through.
10. **Cool and Serve:** Remove from the oven. For an extra touch of flavor and moisture, you can drizzle a little more olive oil over the hot focaccia. Let it cool in the pan for 5-10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Slice and enjoy warm or at room temperature.

## Pro Tips for the Best Focaccia Genovese

Achieving that perfect Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil requires attention to a few key details:

*   **Hydration is Key:** Don't be afraid of a wet, sticky dough. High hydration is what gives Focaccia Genovese its characteristic open, airy crumb. Resist the urge to add too much flour during kneading.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** This cannot be stressed enough. A good extra virgin olive oil imparts flavor, moisture, and contributes significantly to the focaccia's texture and golden crust. Use it generously!
*   **The Dimple Factor:** When dimpling, don't just poke; press firmly all the way down to the bottom of the pan. This creates those essential oil pockets and helps prevent the focaccia from rising too much like a regular loaf of bread.
*   **Don't Rush the Proofing:** Allow the dough ample time to rise. This develops flavor and creates the airy texture. A warm, draft-free environment is ideal.
*   **Hot Oven:** A high oven temperature ensures a quick rise, a crisp exterior, and a well-cooked interior without drying out the bread.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Focaccia

Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is incredibly versatile. Here are some ways to enjoy it:

*   **Simply on its own:** Tear off a piece and savor the flavor. It’s perfect for dipping in a little more extra virgin olive oil or balsamic vinegar.
*   **With Soups or Salads:** A fantastic accompaniment to almost any soup or a fresh, crisp salad.
*   **Appetizer:** Serve alongside a charcuterie board with cheeses, olives, and cured meats.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice horizontally and fill with your favorite ingredients like prosciutto, mozzarella, roasted vegetables, or pesto.
*   **Breakfast or Brunch:** Enjoy with scrambled eggs or alongside a strong cup of coffee.

## Variations and Substitutions for Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil

While the classic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is perfect in its pure form, you can experiment with toppings to suit your taste:

*   **Olives:** Black or green olives, pitted and roughly chopped, pressed into the dimples.
*   **Cherry Tomatoes:** Halved cherry tomatoes, pressed into the dough before baking.
*   **Onions:** Thinly sliced red or white onions, caramelized or fresh, scattered over the top.
*   **Garlic:** Thinly sliced garlic cloves or roasted garlic puree can be added to the dough or sprinkled on top.
*   **Other Herbs:** Thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs can replace or complement the rosemary.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano before baking adds a salty, umami kick.
*   **Sweet Focaccia:** While not traditional Genovese, some regions make sweet focaccia with grapes, sugar, or honey.

Remember, the beauty of this bread lies in its foundation of excellent olive oil, fresh rosemary, and good salt. Any additions should enhance, not overpower, the delicate base.

There's something truly magical about baking bread from scratch, and even more so when that bread is as celebrated and delicious as Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil. From the simple act of mixing flour and water to the intoxicating aroma filling your kitchen as it bakes, every step is a pleasure. This recipe invites you to slow down, engage your senses, and create a piece of culinary art that will transport you straight to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast. So, gather your ingredients, clear your schedule, and prepare to bake a masterpiece that will undoubtedly become a treasured staple in your home.
